documents.body:
# User stories — Programme definition (P0)

## Personas

- **The sponsoring group** — owns the mandate and the business case; accepts the definition set.
- **The SRO / programme manager** — runs the tranches, the plan and the end-of-tranche reviews.
- **The PMO lead** — keeps the registers, the change control and the assurance calendar.
- **The programme architect** — owns the blueprint, the ADM profile and the artefact standard.
- **The BCM** — owns the benefit profiles, the benefits map and realization.
- **The delivery project leads** — T1–T19 and S00–S21 consume the brief template and the inception standard.
- **The public reader** — reads the published definition set on the design site.

## Stories

- As the sponsoring group, I want the mandate, programme brief, blueprint and business case accepted, so that the programme has a contract before T1–T19 start.
- As the programme manager, I want the projects dossier and the tranche plan, so that the 50 projects have a sequence, entry/exit criteria and review dates.
- As the BCM, I want one benefit profile per benefit and a map to each strategic objective, so that realization is measurable.
- As a delivery lead, I want the project brief template and the per-project inception standard, so that my brief and my first two claims are defined.
- As the programme architect, I want the architecture capability baseline — principles, ADM profile, artefact standard, board charter, maturity and skills — so that architecture work is tailored and gated.
- As the public reader, I want the definition set published on the design site, so that the programme's claims are inspectable.

## Scenarios

- Given the seed carried 47 projects and no definition project, when P0 landed, then P0 is a tranche-0 project and T1–T19 carry `blocked_by: [P0]`.
- Given the definition set, when each artefact is composed with its category, then it appears in the record with its own document and public page.
- Given a delivery project blocked by P0, when a run starts, then the start gate refuses until P0 is accepted.
- Given the live tenant, when `projects.create` is invoked for P0, then P0's board exists and the project reads back.
- Given the architecture pack, when the governance chain runs, then every artefact carries the standard's metadata and at least one link.

## Verify

- `cargo test -p conveyor-store seed_programme` — the seed is idempotent and carries P0.
- `python3 scripts/build-coverage.py --check` — P0 is tranche 0 and T1–T19 are `blocked_by: [P0]`.
- `python3 scripts/check-output-standard.py` — the P0 class carries its 21 categories.
- `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --self-test` — the conformance contract holds.
- The published definition set and the P0 pages in `docs/design/docs/standards/`.

## Links

- Plan: `docs/plans/P0-programme-definition.md` §1, §3, §8.
- Units: #120 (project and gate), #121 (definition set), #122 (reuse map and architecture pack).
- Record: the P0 project row and its published outputs.

## Notes

Reconstructed from the programme record on 2026-11-28 for standard v4. The definition set was accepted in tranche 0; this document is the Delivery narrative the standard asks for, not a new claim.

documents.title: Acceptance criteria — Programme definition (P0)
documents.body:
# Acceptance criteria — Programme definition (P0)

## Scenarios

- P0 exists as a tranche-0 project and T1–T19 are `blocked_by: [P0]`.
- The definition set is published on P0 with the P0 class's 21 categories.
- A delivery project blocked by P0 cannot start before acceptance.
- P0's board exists on the live tenant and reads back.
- The programme plan lists 50 projects with tranches and dependencies.
- Every benefit has a profile with baseline, target, method and owner, and at least one map path to a strategic objective.
- Every tranche has entry and exit criteria and a review date.
- Every delivery brief carries reuse sources and the two inception units.
- The architecture capability baseline is published on P0.
- Every architecture artefact carries the standard's metadata and at least one link.
- The Validation page shows P0 at tranche 0 and T1–T19 `blocked_by: [P0]`.

## Verify commands

- `cargo test -p conveyor-store seed_programme`
- `python3 scripts/build-coverage.py --check`
- `python3 scripts/check-output-standard.py`
- `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --self-test`
- The live board read-back recorded on #120.
- The public-page checks recorded on #121 and #122.

## Results

Met at the P0 baseline and re-checked by the tranche-0 retrospective rework. #120, #121 and #122 are closed; P0 is `measured_status: built` and `status: closed`; the definition documents and the architecture pack are in the record. The live board and page checks recorded on the issues passed. The one act the plan leaves to the sponsoring group — the first-tranche authorisation (`tranche-review`) — is recorded by the programme, not by P0.

## Status

met — the three units closed and the definition set published; the tranche review remains the sponsoring group's act.

## Links

- Plan §8; #120, #121, #122; the P0 project row.

documents.title: Definition of ready — Programme definition (P0)
documents.body:
# Definition of ready — Programme definition (P0)

## Independent

The three units are file-disjoint: #120 changes the seed and coverage; #121 authors the definition documents; #122 authors the reuse map and the architecture pack. P0 has no incoming dependency; T1–T19 depend on it.

## Negotiable

The outcome is fixed — the definition set accepted and the programme unblocked. The document set and the order of the three units were settled at delivery.

## Valuable

P0 removes the named gap: the programme had no definition project and T1–T19 could not start. It maps to B6 — the register, the audit and the published scorecard agree at every tranche review — and to the definition set's own acceptance.

## Estimable

Baseline `main` at the P0 claim; the plan, the seed and the three units name every file. The plan's §8 acceptance is the measured target.

## Small

One issue per unit, one branch and one PR each; #120, #121 and #122 are the three units.

## Testable

Every part of each unit carries a Given/When/Then scenario with a `Verify:` command; the plan §8 acceptance is the project-level test.

## Dependencies

- blocked-by: none — P0 has `depends_on: []`.
- blocks: T1–T19, through the start gate.
- related: the programme definition set and the architecture capability baseline.

## Notes

Reconstructed for standard v4 on 2026-11-28; the project's closed state is the record's.

documents.body:
# Definition of done — Programme definition (P0)

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Verify |
|---|---|
| P0 is a tranche-0 project and T1–T19 are `blocked_by: [P0]` | `cargo test -p conveyor-store seed_programme`; `python3 scripts/build-coverage.py --check` |
| The definition set is published with the P0 class's 21 categories | `python3 scripts/check-output-standard.py`; the P0 pages in the pack |
| A delivery project blocked by P0 cannot start | the #120 gate scenario |
| P0's board exists on the live tenant | the #120 live read-back |
| The plan §8 rows (50 projects, benefit profiles, tranche criteria, briefs, architecture baseline, artefact metadata, Validation page) | the pack and governance-chain checks on #121 and #122 |

## Evidence at completion

#120, #121 and #122 are closed. P0 is `measured_status: built` and `status: closed`; the definition documents and the architecture pack are in the record. The live board read-back and the public-page checks are recorded on the issues.

## Repo gate

The units' gates: the seed test, `build-coverage.py --check`, `check-output-standard.py`, the pack checks and `build-docs.py --check`. The plan §8 acceptance is green. The historical #120 DoD names `rbuild`; that route is retired — the compile/lint verdict is the repository's preflight and its PR CI.

## Merge and closure

Each unit closed by its PR; P0 closed at tranche 0; the branches deleted. The tranche review is the sponsoring group's separate act.

## Links

- Plan §8; #120, #121, #122; the P0 project row.
